centroid_terminology_clarification: This probe estimates two domain centroids from the 35 non-held-out independent source groups for each fold. It is a fitted descriptive nearest-centroid classifier, with no neural-network training, optimizer updates or held-out group leakage. The executable definition phrase no fitted model means no additional learned neural model; this clarification controls interpretation.

cpu_tests.runtime: Pinned AutoDL Python3.12.3, CPU; no model forward

execution_exceptions.resolution: Independent new code_git_protocol packet uses exact historical Git blob. Original packet and protocols retained; second precheck PASS before the sole forward run.

interpretation: Context domain predictability is a risk signal on a selected 36-group TRAIN sample, not proof of a pure style shortcut or a population estimate.
Target domain predictability can reflect intended defect removal as well as generation/registration differences; do not interpret target separation alone as artifacts.
Laplacian variance ratios above one indicate changed high-frequency energy, not a calibrated blur quality score. Registration, resampling, sharpening and noise can contribute.
Perimeter absolute error is a seam-adjacent change proxy; intended restoration and structural displacement are confounded.
No diagnostic score approves, rejects or ranks cases for human G1. Unannotated context is not normal GT.

P3 receptive fields can cross excluded masks: context feature changes can still reflect intended target removal even when context pooling pixels exclude annotated/edit support. Five-pixel exclusion does not isolate causal style.

The frozen representation was trained on these original TRAIN members. Group holding out applies only to the descriptive centroid probe, not to representation pretraining; this is not held-out predictive validation.
